nodes.label: Broken Access Control (OWASP A01)
nodes.rationale: Multiple reviews found publication status and ownership checks bypassed at the API layer, so the database is never asked to enforce visibility.

nodes.label: Row Level Security policy
nodes.rationale: Reviews want RLS as the last line of defense: deny-by-default, service-role-only for operational auth tables, so a flaw in route-level authorization cannot read or write everything.

nodes.label: CSRF token verification
nodes.rationale: SameSite=Lax alone is treated as insufficient for cookie-authenticated state-changing admin APIs; a CSRF middleware already exists so the missing call is a defense layer gap.

nodes.label: Rate limiting / abuse control
nodes.rationale: Unauthenticated public endpoints (news, search, suggest, wishlist) allow trivial bulk scraping and DB load amplification; authorization alone does not give abuse resistance on admin routes.

nodes.label: Audit logging
nodes.rationale: Privileged content mutations (news, look, stockist) leave no durable trail, blocking incident investigation and publication-history review.

nodes.label: Sensitive auth token / cookie logging
nodes.rationale: Even partial token disclosure lowers attack cost when logs are centrally retained; the shared Supabase server helper puts this leak on every page and API path.

nodes.label: Public storage bucket exposure
nodes.rationale: Buckets are created public while row visibility is governed by status + RLS, so unpublished assets stay internet-reachable and break the publication boundary.

nodes.label: Private bucket + signed URL delivery
nodes.rationale: Proposed fix for public buckets: private storage with signed URLs, or move objects between draft and published buckets at publish time.

nodes.label: Service role client bypasses RLS
nodes.rationale: Admin and wishlist APIs always use createServiceRoleClient(), so DB policies never act as the final gate; reviews recommend request-scoped clients or narrow RPCs.

nodes.label: Auth tokens exposed to client-side JavaScript
nodes.rationale: Tokens returned in JSON and persisted in localStorage make one XSS enough to steal a long-lived session, contradicting the HttpOnly cookie design.

nodes.label: HttpOnly/Secure cookie session model
nodes.rationale: Design docs 14_login.md and 01_auth_seq.md require server-set HttpOnly cookies as the sole refresh transport.

nodes.label: Server-managed OAuth state / PKCE flow
nodes.rationale: Client-side signInWithOAuth plus exchangeCodeForSession bypasses DB-backed replay protection, audit coverage, server-controlled redirects, and the account-link policy.

nodes.label: Refresh token reuse / replay detection
nodes.rationale: A stolen refresh token should trigger quarantine, full session revocation, and an audit event rather than best-effort row replacement.

nodes.label: Reset token delivered as URL query parameter
nodes.rationale: Tokens in the URL persist in browser history, screenshots, and copied links; the design requires server-side one-time consumption plus a clean redirect.

nodes.label: Host header poisoning via forwarded headers
nodes.rationale: getRequestOrigin() trusts x-forwarded-host / x-forwarded-proto unconditionally, letting an attacker rewrite confirmation-mail and redirect origins.

nodes.label: Email marked confirmed without ownership proof
nodes.rationale: JIT creation with email_confirm: true breaks downstream email_verified assumptions and leaves confirmed accounts after typos or misdelivery.

nodes.label: PostgREST filter grammar injection
nodes.rationale: Not SQL injection, but unescaped ',' and ')' in .or() strings let a caller alter search conditions and observe error-based behavior.

nodes.label: Rate limiter fails open on datastore error
nodes.rationale: An attacker who can break counter persistence, or a DB outage, disables brute-force protection on auth endpoints entirely.

nodes.label: Zod input validation
nodes.rationale: Search validation only trims and caps length; the spec's forbidden-character/400 rule and control-character rejection are unimplemented.

nodes.label: Publication status filter (status = published)
nodes.rationale: Explicit status filtering is required wherever service-role or joined access can bypass RLS, notably wishlist item joins and published looks linked to private items.

nodes.label: session_id cookie survives logout
nodes.rationale: The 30-day httpOnly session_id is neither cleared nor rotated at logout, so a shared browser hands the previous user's wishlist to the next user.

nodes.label: React automatic escaping (XSS control)
nodes.rationale: Every page review found no dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink; React text nodes are what currently prevents stored/reflected XSS, so introducing rich-text HTML would require re-review.

nodes.label: Unconditional third-party script loading
nodes.rationale: Turnstile and a jsDelivr stylesheet load on every route including static policy pages, sending page-view metadata to third parties without SRI pinning.

nodes.label: CSP and security headers
nodes.rationale: Static pages like /terms have no defenses of their own; their protection comes entirely from proxy-level CSP and headers, so matcher regressions silently widen exposure.

hyperedges.label: Auth tokens escaping the HttpOnly cookie boundary
Public storage buckets breaking the publication boundary
Unauthenticated public APIs without rate limiting or audit
